human_tolerance.notes: Attracted to back gardens in Europe and North America by birdfeeders containing niger (nyjer) seed; special polycarbonate feeders with small slits are sometimes used just for this species. Not as tightly bound to buildings as the house sparrow (it nests in trees, not building cavities), so treated as an Adapter rather than an Exploiter.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: The parents typically raise two broods each year and occasionally three; incubation is 11-13 days and nestlings fledge 13-18 days after hatching. Exact start/end dates are a judgement placed around the described breeding activity, matching a typical UK finch breeding season.

phases.name: flocking
phases.note: 'During this time [winter], European goldfinches group together to form flocks of up to 40, and occasionally more' and regularly visit bird feeders; exact boundary dates are a judgement.

vocalizations.description: Melodic contact call, described as a 'tickeLIT', given while flying, perched or feeding in flocks.
Pleasant silvery twittering: a tinkling medley of trills and twitters that always includes the tri-syllabic call phrase, a 'teLLIT-teLLIT-teLLIT'.

No distinct alarm call is documented for this species in the cited source; authored as a sharper, more rapidly repeated version of the 'tickeLIT' contact call, a pattern typical of small flocking finches warning of danger.

common_names.note: en/fr/de/nl labels from Wikidata sitelink titles (frwiki/dewiki/nlwiki).

conservation.note: Wikidata P141 (IUCN conservation status) = least concern.

range.note: `introduced` is a direct list from Wikipedia's Distribution section ('introduced to Bermuda, Canada, the United States, Mexico, Peru, Argentina, Chile, the Falkland Islands, Uruguay, Brazil, South Africa, Australia, and New Zealand in the 19th century'). `native` is derived from the subspecies range descriptions in the Taxonomy section (Britain; most of the European mainland and Scandinavia; Iberia, NW Africa and Macaronesia; Corsica/Sardinia/Sicily; the Balkans, Greece, Crete and NW Turkey; Rhodes, Karpathos, Cyprus, Egypt to Asia Minor, N Iraq, SW Iran, and NE Africa; E Turkey, S Caucasus and NW Iran; Crimea and N Caucasus; S Ukraine, SW Russia and NW Kazakhstan; W Siberia), excluding the caniceps subspecies group split off in 2023 as the separate grey-crowned goldfinch (their South/Central Asian range is not included here).

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Ground locomotion is not explicitly described in the cited source; hopping (rather than walking) is family-typical for small perching finches, by analogy with the house sparrow record in this repository.

traits.nest_type.note: 'The neat, compact nest is usually located several metres above the ground ... It is made of moss and lichen ... A deep cup prevents eggs from being lost in windy weather.'

traits.mass_kg.note: Midpoint of 'weighs 14 to 19 g (0.49 to 0.67 oz)'.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of 'average European goldfinch is 12-13 cm (4.7-5.1 in) long'.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Wikidata P2050 (wingspan) = 0.24 m; consistent with Wikipedia's 'wingspan of 21-25 cm (8.3-9.8 in)'.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No sourced typical or mean lifespan figure was found for this species on Wikipedia, Wikidata or GBIF (Wikidata carries no longevity property for this item, and a literature search turned up only a note that ringing sample sizes are too small for a robust BTO survival estimate for this species). Estimated by analogy to similarly sized European garden passerines already in this repository with a sourced figure (house sparrow ~2.2 y, European robin ~1.1 y), both of which show high first-year mortality typical of small songbirds; 2.0 y is used as a conservative, unsourced judgement pending a better source.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 10, Diet-Fruit 20, Diet-Seed 40, Diet-PlantO 30 (BirdFuncDat row for Carduelis carduelis). The schema has no generic 'other plant material' bucket, so Diet-Fruit and Diet-PlantO are combined into the schema's 'fruit' share (10/40/50), as this record's closest worked example (house sparrow) also does. Consistent with Wikipedia: 'preferred food is small seeds ... but it also eats insects when it feeds its young.'

traits.social.note: 'European goldfinches group together to form flocks of up to 40, and occasionally more' outside the breeding season. group_size lower bound is a judgement (pairs/small family groups in the breeding season).

traits.activity_pattern.note: EltonTraits Nocturnal=0; a diurnal, day-feeding finch.

traits.defense.note: Authored: a small, flocking finch with no described active defence; flees from disturbance like other small garden passerines in this repository.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: regularly visits garden bird feeders (niger seed) and tolerates people at some distance, but nests in trees rather than in or on buildings and is not described as approaching people as closely as the house sparrow, so given a higher wariness than that record's 0.15.

habitat.use.note: ForStrat-ground 20, ForStrat-understory 60, ForStrat-midhigh 20 (understory+midhigh mapped to arboreal).

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Nests and roosts in trees and shrubs ('the end of a swaying branch ... hidden by leaves and twigs').

habitat.resources.note: Seed/fruit weights follow the EltonTraits-derived diet shares; invertebrate use is restricted to the breeding season and the Juvenile stage per Wikipedia ('a mixture of seeds and insects, but as they grow the proportion of insect material decreases'); nest_cup, perch and shrub_thicket weights are a judgement matching the tree/shrub nesting and roosting behaviour described.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: urban_affinity and uses_gardens from the described garden feeder behaviour; light_max is a judgement.

seasonal.strategy.note: 'It ... is resident in the milder western regions of its habitat, but migrates from colder areas.' Great Britain is in the milder, resident part of the range, so ActiveYearRound is used for the GB record; birds elsewhere in the range are migratory or partially migratory, per the source.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding biology (nest-building, incubation, fledging, two-to-three broods) and winter flocking behaviour are from Wikipedia; the exact phase start/end dates are judgement.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Nestlings fledge 13-18 days after hatching and are fed by both parents for a further 7-9 days; duration_days and scale are a judgement approximation from these figures, not a sourced figure.

vocalizations.alarm.note: Authored: no distinct alarm call is documented in the cited source; modelled on the sharper alarm-context call other small perching songbirds in this repository are given.

look.note: Plumage: red face with black markings around the eyes, black-and-white head, buff/chestnut-brown back and flanks, black wings with a broad yellow bar, black tail, white rump, ivory pointed bill. Proportions and extra-part placement are judgement.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared perching-songbird program: seed-based foraging, a nest built several metres up in a tree (nest_m1/nest_m2), and a flee distance in line with a species that visits feeders but is more easily flushed than a house sparrow.
